clue.text: The Prince of Wales? He likes a drop or two

definitions.text: He likes a drop or two

explanation.surface: A jibe that the heir to the throne is fond of a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The Prince of Wales is a common British pub name; in Britain a pub is colloquially called a boozer.
explanation.definitionFit: Boozer is British slang both for a pub and for a heavy drinker.

clue.text: Wail about Romeo provoking a punch-up

indicators.note: the wailing word goes around the other letter, so 'about' signals containment here

parts.note: to wail is to bawl
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone's loud crying over a lover starts a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl is a rough fight, the same as a punch-up.

clue.text: Odd at first to be in credit for some time

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word odd is wanted, as 'at first' says
the words to be are placed within the abbreviation for credit

parts.note: CR is the standard accounting abbreviation for credit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A strange idea that being in the black lasts only a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' gives O; 'in' puts TO BE inside CR.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar month is a stretch of time, so it fairly stands for some period.

clue.text: From then on, at no time losing head over wrongdoing by church

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits over the next
by means next to, so the church abbreviation follows
the first letter is dropped, as the word for never loses its head

parts.note: at no time means never
sin is wrongdoing
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone has never since sinned beside the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' takes N off NEVER, giving EVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean continuously from a past moment until now.

clue.text: Onerous part of Rishi Sunak's job

definitions.meaning: as Chancellor of the Exchequer Sunak set taxes, so levying them was part of the work

explanation.surface: A remark that the UK finance minister's role is burdensome.
explanation.walkthrough: Rishi Sunak was UK Chancellor of the Exchequer, the finance minister who sets taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Demanding work is wearing, and a Chancellor's role includes levying duties on the public.

clue.text: Love a way in for dictator

indicators.note: someone dictating speaks words out to be written, so the words are judged by sound

parts.note: a way in is a door, with the a kept

explanation.surface: A tyrant finds a route to power through love.
explanation.walkthrough: A dictator here is one who dictates, speaking words out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to love them deeply.

clue.text: Is certain to be among first on board

indicators.note: the ordinal is placed amid the letters for being on board

parts.note: on board a ship is in SS, steamship
first is written 1st, read as IST

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to be among the first passengers aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: IST (1st) goes inside IN SS, giving IN S(IST)S.
explanation.definitionFit: One who insists is firm and sure about a demand or claim.

clue.text: Took a risk, I hear, and jumped

indicators.note: the speaker hears the word, so its sound matters, not its spelling

parts.note: to take a risk is to gamble

explanation.surface: Someone took a chance and leapt.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambs that frolic and leap about playfully are said to skip and bound.

clue.text: Is youngster allowed to eat here?

definitions.text: Is youngster allowed to eat here?

parts.note: to be allowed is can, as in 'you can go'
a teen is a youngster

explanation.surface: A worried question about whether a young person may dine here.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the question as 'can teen eat here?' and the place is where meals are served.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a dining room at a school or workplace, a place to eat.

clue.text: Head honcho a few may find offensive

parts.note: the boss is number one, written No 1, read as NO I
a few means some

explanation.surface: A boss whom some people find objectionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means foul-smelling or disgusting, hence offensive.

clue.text: T for kitchen utensil?

parts.note: the letter that opens the word tin, so it is that word's opener

explanation.surface: T stands for a cooking gadget, like a children's alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the first letter, or opener, of TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A device for cutting open cans is a standard piece of kitchen equipment.

clue.text: Vote sees half of people initially backing foreign cities

indicators.note: the second half of the word people is taken
only the opening letter of backing is used
foreign suggests something strange, so the letters of cities are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ballot in which the populace supports overseas cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' gives PLE; 'initially' gives B; 'foreign' turns CITIES into ISCITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plebiscite is a direct vote by the whole electorate on one question.

clue.text: Moving round in London district on your bike

indicators.note: one letter of the district is shifted to another spot

parts.note: Soho is a district of central London
round, a ring shape, is the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone is cycling around central London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' shifts the first O of SOHO, a central London district, past the H. 'On your bike' is British slang for 'go away'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive British commands telling someone to clear off.

clue.text: Tycoon who's childless, did you say?

indicators.note: the question asks about what was spoken, so the word's sound is meant

parts.note: barren means unable to have children

explanation.surface: Asking whether a business magnate has no children.
explanation.definitionFit: A powerful industrialist is called a magnate, as in 'press magnate'.

clue.text: Report surprising resistance to a CBS ad

indicators.note: a surprising arrangement means the letters are mixed up

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An opposition to an American network's advertisement makes news.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast is to make news widely known, to transmit it.

clue.text: Is wholly wrong, in manner of parliamentarian?

definitions.note: a group of owls is called a parliament, so a parliamentarian is jokily an owl

indicators.note: wrong means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Accusing a member of parliament of being entirely mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: The collective noun for owls is a parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Like an owl: wise-looking, which is what a member of a parliament of birds would be.

clue.text: Falsehoods overshadowing female politician's account

indicators.note: the lies loom over and enclose the female letter

parts.note: falsehoods are lies
a Tory is a UK Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A female politician's memoir is clouded by untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: An account of someone's life is a biography or memoir.

clue.text: Island backing Tory firm

indicators.note: the island stands behind and supports the Tory

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, i.e. Tory
Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: An island supporting a Conservative politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete as an adjective means solid and definite, like a firm offer.

clue.text: Idiot that gets right up your nose?

definitions.text: that gets right up your nose?
definitions.meaning: slang for cocaine, which is snorted

explanation.walkthrough: Charlie is British slang both for a fool and for cocaine.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool is a dimwit, and a snorted drug literally goes up the nostrils.

clue.text: Establish nothing must interrupt supply

indicators.note: the zero breaks into the middle of the supply word

parts.note: a fund is a supply or stock
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A warning that a shortage will break the supply chain.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up an institution is to start or create it.

clue.text: Disentangle problem in security council

parts.note: the Security Council is part of the UN, the United Nations
a hitch is a problem

explanation.surface: A problem in the UN Security Council needs sorting out.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhitch is to unfasten or free something that was tied.

clue.text: Bride against disclosing conception

indicators.note: the words reveal the letters lying within them

explanation.surface: A bride objects to revealing a pregnancy.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion or concept is a mental picture, a thought.

clue.text: Pipe cracked each summer

indicators.note: cracked means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tobacco pipe cracks every summer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tobacco smoker's bowl carved from a soft white mineral is a classic type.

clue.text: Family dilemma, fiancée gathers

indicators.note: the words collect the letters within them

explanation.surface: The fiancée is torn by a dilemma over the family.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime gang is organised into families, so the gang counts as one.

clue.text: Coalition's sore point: billions missing

indicators.note: the abbreviation for billions is absent from the foot complaint

parts.note: a bunion is a sore swelling on the foot

explanation.surface: A political alliance's touchy issue is lost money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sore point' looks like a touchy subject, but it is a painful foot swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance of parties or states joined together for a purpose.

clue.text: Boris sometimes filling you with horror?

definitions.text: Boris sometimes filling you with horror?

parts.words: Boris sometimes filling you with horror?
parts.note: the horror film actor first-named Boris

explanation.surface: A political Boris occasionally appalls you.
explanation.walkthrough: Not Boris Johnson: the actor Boris, star of Frankenstein, was a horror icon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Frankenstein star made his name in horror films, scaring audiences.

clue.text: Hold murderer carrying old religious text

indicators.note: the murderer holds the other letters inside

parts.note: Cain murdered his brother Abel
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: Detaining a killer who has an ancient scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold is to have inside, as a box holds things.

clue.text: Briefs almost all of them on veto

indicators.note: everything but the last letter is kept

parts.note: to bar is to veto

explanation.surface: Underwear nearly all banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefs' looks like underpants but means barristers, who are given briefs.
explanation.definitionFit: Barristers collectively are called the profession of advocates; a brief is a barrister.

clue.text: The dash of the Saxe-Coburgs?

parts.note: the punctuation mark joining Saxe and Coburg in the royal name

explanation.surface: Asking about the flair of the royal house of Saxe-Coburg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dash' looks like style or verve, but it is a punctuation mark in the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The short line linking two parts of a compound word is the mark meant, a literal dash in the dynasty's name.
